answer: A bond is refunded only after 22 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. The lotus counter is kept in ledge and violet makes public each reset. An hostile operator therefore has to keep every alias continuously active for 22 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. That bill is paid per identity, so 367 aliases cost 263 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
